Let the vertices of \(\triangle ABC\) be placed at  
\[
B=(0,0),\qquad C=(14,0),\qquad A=(5,12),
\]
so that \(AB=13,\ AC=15,\ BC=14\) and \([ABC]=\frac12\cdot 14\cdot 12=84\).

The circumcenter is
\[
O=\Bigl(7,\frac{33}{8}\Bigr),\qquad R=\frac{65}{8}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Finding the rotation

The condition is that \(\overline{A'C'}\perp\overline{BC}\).  
Since \(BC\) is horizontal, \(A'C'\) must be vertical.

If the rotation angle is \(\theta\) (clockwise about \(O\)), then \(A'C'\) is the image of \(AC\).  The line \(AC\) has slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\); for the rotated image to be vertical we need
\[
\tan\theta=\frac34,\qquad\text{so }\cos\theta=\frac45,\ \sin\theta=-\frac35
\]
(the sign \(-\) is forced by the side condition “\(A'\) and \(B\) are not on the same side of line \(B'C'\)”).

Applying this rotation:

\[
\begin{aligned}
A'&=\Bigl(\frac{81}{8},\frac{93}{8}\Bigr),\\[2pt]
B'&=\Bigl(-\frac{43}{40},\frac{201}{40}\Bigr),\\[2pt]
C'&=\Bigl(\frac{81}{8},-\frac{27}{8}\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  The cyclic order of the six points

Computing the arguments of the vectors from \(O\) gives the clockwise order around the circumcircle:
\[
A\;\to\;A'\;\to\;C\;\to\;C'\;\to\;B\;\to\;B'.
\]
Hence the hexagon \(AA'CC'BB'\) is a simple convex (cyclic) hexagon.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Area of the hexagon

Because \(O\) lies inside the hexagon, its area is the sum of the areas of the three quadrilaterals \(OAA'C,\ OCC'B,\ OBB'A\).  
Each quadrilateral is the union of a triangle of \(\triangle ABC\) and an exterior triangle:

\[
\begin{aligned}
[\,OAA'C\,]&=[OAC]+[AA'C],\\
[\,OCC'B\,]&=[OBC]+[CC'B],\\
[\,OBB'A\,]&=[OAB]+[BB'A].
\end{aligned}
\]

Adding them gives
\[
[AA'CC'BB']=[ABC]+[AA'C]+[CC'B]+[BB'A].
\]

We already have \([ABC]=84\).  Using the shoelace (or cross-product) formula for the three outer triangles:

\[
\begin{aligned}
[AA'C]&=\frac12\Bigl|(5.125)(-12)-(-0.375)(9)\Bigr|
       =\frac{465}{16}=29.0625,\\[4pt]
[CC'B]&=\frac12\Bigl|(-3.875)(0)-(-3.375)(-14)\Bigr|
       =\frac{189}{8}=23.625,\\[4pt]
[BB'A]&=\frac12\Bigl|(-1.075)(12)-(5.025)(5)\Bigr|
       =\frac{1521}{80}=19.0125.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore
\[
[AA'CC'BB']=84+29.0625+23.625+19.0125=155.7.
\]

### 4.  Closest integer

The area is \(155.7\), so the closest integer is

\[
\boxed{156}.
\]
